definitions.explanation: A round bamboo or wooden basket with a slatted bottom used for steaming food over a pot of boiling water. Used both in Japanese cuisine (steamed buns, vegetables, seafood) and in Chinese dim sum.

examples.japanese: {蒸籠|せいろ}で{野菜|やさい}を{蒸|む}した。
examples.english: I steamed vegetables in a bamboo steamer.

examples.japanese: {蒸籠|せいろ}を{重|かさ}ねて{何|なん}{種類|しゅるい}もの{点心|てんしん}を{一度|いちど}に{蒸|む}せる。
examples.english: You can stack the steamers and steam several kinds of dim sum at once.

examples.japanese: {蒸籠|せいろ}は{使|つか}った{後|あと}に{完全|かんぜん}に{乾|かわ}かさないとカビが{生|は}えやすい。
examples.english: If you don't dry the bamboo steamer thoroughly after use, it tends to get mouldy.

notes:
Originally a Chinese cooking implement; now also fully integrated into Japanese kitchens. The kanji {蒸籠|せいろ} is rarely written by hand — the kana spelling せいろ is more common in everyday writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {蒸籠|せいろ}で{蒸|む}す: to steam in a bamboo steamer
- {蒸籠|せいろ}を{重|かさ}ねる: to stack steamers
- {蒸籠|せいろ}{蒸|む}し: a dish steamed in a bamboo steamer

RELATED USE:
The word also names a soba dish: {蒸籠|せいろ}そば, cold soba noodles served on a bamboo tray — historically the noodles were once steamed, hence the name.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {蒸|む}し{器|き}: steamer (general) — metal multi-tiered steamers, not specifically bamboo
